subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a static vehicle model, using a builder pattern with box helpers to construct the geometry without joints, and now sketching out the truck's dimensions.

Designing the layout: an 8x8 military truck with four axles, a forward cab, armored hull, and a rear weapon pod featuring a railgun turret, missile racks, sensor mast, and detail elements like exhaust stacks, light bars, and neon underglow. I'm setting up helper functions for boxes and cylinders with rotation support and a glow effect, plus a gunmetal and magenta/cyan color palette.

Working out wheel placement across four axles so the lowest wheel sits at ground level, with fenders boxed in above each wheel arch.

Still working out wheel geometry...

Now I'm designing the cab: a lower body box, an upper cabin section, and a sloped windshield built from a thin rotated box positioned at the front, giving it a glowing cyan look.

Working out the windshield as a thin tilted box, rotating it about the X-axis so it leans back at roughly a 62° angle to match the slope from the hood to the cabin roof.

Instead of stacking separate flat panels for the cab, I'm realizing it'd be simpler to build the whole cabin silhouette as a single extruded shape from a side-profile outline, which avoids gaps at the triangular side windows.

I'm calculating the windshield tilt angle at roughly 62 degrees, then adding glowing cyan side window boxes and a front bumper box to round out the car's geometry.

Now I'm detailing the front fascia with hazard stripes, a dark grille with magenta glowing slits, angled headlight bars, and a plow wedge underneath, then moving to the roof: armor plating, a light bar, antennas, a sensor dome, a small remote weapon turret, and smoke launcher tubes.

Next I'm adding mirror arms by the cab, angular side armor skirts with bolted hex plates, and designing the rear hull bed module with a sloped profile outline and panel greeble details on the sides.

Now I'm adding ribbed panels with neon magenta and cyan strips, hazard stripes on the rear, and building the top turret ring, body, and railgun with parallel rails, making sure the barrel clears the cab roof height.

Working out the railgun details: barrel length, rail positioning, glowing capacitor coil rings along the barrel, muzzle brake, breech block, ammo box and antenna at the turret rear. I'm also placing missile pods on either side of the rear roof with angled tube holes.

Now adding rear details -- fuel/battery tanks, vertical exhaust stacks with glowing orange caps, a rear bumper, red taillight bars, and a ramp. Underneath I'm sketching the drive shaft, differential spheres, axle cylinders at specific wheel positions, and leaf springs, while considering whether to fit side fuel tanks between the wheel gaps.

Working through the side tank placement and dimensions to avoid wheel overlap, then starting on fender slabs sized to sit over each wheel.

Adding thin magenta underglow strips beneath the body. For labeling, I'll generate a textured decal plane with "2077" stenciled text via an SVG texture, placing it on the door facing outward so it reads correctly from both sides.

Now I'm adding more decal text like "MIL-TRK 7" and considering glowing hologram stencil panels, with the text itself emitting a magenta/cyan glow against a transparent background. I'm also working out hull width placement so the rear and cab extrusions align at the correct x-offsets, aiming for roughly 250 parts total built through loops with varied flat-color materials.

Writing helper functions...

Still detailing the wheel geometry...

Now I'm thinking through the fender flares for the wheel arches, positioning box shapes alongside the tire's upper curve so they clear the body underside while covering the tire's side profile.

For the axles, I'm setting z positions at 2.6, 1.0, -1.6, -3.2 for the four wheel stations, with the front two visually steerable. I'm placing cylinder axle segments rotated 90 degrees running through each wheel hub, checking that the cab body and fender flares don't intersect with the wheel geometry at each position.

Still placing details...

Working out the hood slope angle, I set it to tilt 20 degrees so it rotates and positions correctly. Then I'm adding tinted glass side windows on the cab at both sides with a soft cyan glow rim, and considering a rear cabin window near the hull.

Now I'm sketching out door seams as thin vertical dark boxes, handles, lower armor slab plates on the cab sides, and thinking about whether to add yellow chevron accents or skip hazard striping for an emblem instead. Then I'm building the roof panel with rails and a small light bar made of alternating cyan and magenta glow boxes along the top.

Next I'm placing twin antennas with red glow tips, a sensor dome sphere mounted with a base cylinder on the roof, and a tilted radar dish made from a flattened cone plus a rod, positioning it off-center so it clears the railgun's path over the roof. I'm adding mirror arms with small mirror boxes, and starting to think about smoke launchers near the front of the cab.

Adding rib details, glowing neon strips, and a roof deck plate with hatches...

Now I'm shaping the turret ring and body, defining its extruded profile outline positioned at the back of the hull.

Still working out the cannon assembly — adding a mantlet box, breech, and twin rail barrels extending forward over the truck's hood at a length that clears the cab roof.

Adding more turret details...

Adding rear hull details now: tail lights as red glow bars near the rear slope, a rear bumper box at the chassis end, and positioning the sloped outline transition between the vertical rear face and the angled roof section.

I'm also working out exhaust stack placement behind the cab, checking that it clears the fender flare and wheel well without overlapping the hull's upper edge.

Then I'm adding bracket boxes attaching the stacks to the hull, a cap and glowing orange ring at the top, and a heat shield. Underneath I'm placing a driveshaft cylinder running along the z-axis under the chassis, plus side fuel tanks positioned further out.

Still placing underbody details... I'm adding yellow accent bands, deciding to skip rear battery boxes between the wheels, and planning the cab floor between the axles. I'm also adding magenta underglow strips and cross strips below the chassis, and sketching a door emblem texture with a "2077" text design.

Now I'm working out where to place armor plates and emblems on the sides -- figuring out x-offsets for the cab lower side, armor slabs, and emblem placement on either the side face or rear hull panel, while checking for collisions with the rib spacing along the hull.

I'm spacing ribs down the hull at regular z intervals, then leaving a gap between two of them to fit a "2077" emblem with bold glowing text, sizing the plane and texture resolution for it.

Skipping extra cab chevrons and ladders to keep things simple, but I'll add hazard stripes up front, chevron boxes on the rear, spotlights on the cab roof corners, and a satellite dish with feed rod on the rear deck.

Positioning the missile pods and dish, confirming tire bottoms sit at ground level and the plow wedge clears above zero, then adding side skirts, a few glowing antenna tips, and a spinning LiDAR unit with a glow ring on the roof before writing the final meta and export code.

Choosing a militarized color palette with dark olive-grey hull panels, steel and glass accents, and bright cyan/magenta highlights for a cyberpunk-military look.

Writing tread block loops...

Finalizing the code now, keeping it clean and avoiding unused variables.
